newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Two Pakistani provincial governors replaced.
newsitem.headline: Two Pakistani provincial governors replaced.

text.p: Pakistani President Farooq Leghari has replaced two provincial governors with high court chief justices, a presidential spokesman said on Wednesday.
He said Leghari had asked Punjab governor Raja Saroop Khan, a known loyalist of former minister Benazir Bhutto, to resign on Tuesday.
He had also accepted the resignation of North West Frontier Province (NWFP) governor, Khursheed Ali Khan, who was said to have asked earlier to be relieved of his post on health grounds.
"The chief justices of the provincial high courts have replaced them," the spokesman said.
Leghari sacked Bhutto's three-year-old government on Tuesday, saying it was tainted with corruption, nepotism and misrule.

There was no word on whether the four provincial assemblies in Punjab, Sindh, Balochistan and NWFP would be dissolved. But the spokesman said a decision might emerge at the first meeting of new caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid's cabinet on Wednesday.
Political analysts said it would be strange if the provincial assemblies survived, following Leghari's order on Tuesday dissolving the National Assembly (lower house).
He set February 3 as the date for fresh parliamentary elections and appointed Khalid as head of a three-month caretaker government to supervise them.
